title: Your day, in detail
job: Longer habitual narration with sequencing words
verifiedBy: LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedPatterns: Mi alzo + , + mi lavo + e + mi vesto

rules.text: A REFLEXIVE VERB IS MARKED TWICE IN ITALIAN AND ONCE IN ENGLISH. The pronoun comes BEFORE the verb and changes with the person, and the ending changes with it: mi alzo, ti alzi, si alza, ci alziamo, vi alzate, si alzano. English says "I get up" with nothing marked at all, so the Italian pronoun looks like a spare word and gets dropped. It is not optional and it is not "myself": it is part of the verb.

The reflexive pronouns are words the course already owns doing a second job. mi and ti are L2-M5's, si is L2-M4's, ci is L2-M6's ci vediamo. Say this out loud rather than meeting mi twice by accident: here mi points the verb back at its own subject, and in L3-M5 the same mi will be an object. One family of little words, two jobs — not two families.

MAI NEEDS NON. Italian requires the second negative where English forbids it: non mangio mai, never *mangio mai. The course showed this shape already in non c'era nessuno; here it is stated as the rule. non goes in front of the verb, mai after it, and the sentence is only negative when both are present.

Frequency words have a home. di solito, qualche volta and ogni + a day FRAME the sentence and go at the front; spesso, sempre, raramente and mai colour the verb and sit right after it. Nothing agrees and nothing changes shape, so the whole cost of this set is where to put it.

The sequencing spine is nearly free: prima and dopo are L2-M4's direction words doing a time job, poi is L1-M10's, and infine is the only new one. None of them is a verb and none of them needs a preposition, so a day can be laid out end to end without another piece of grammar.

Speech elides where this course does not. An Italian says m'alzo and writes mi alzo, and rung writes ONE spelling per display, always the full one, always with a straight apostrophe. Where an elided form is genuinely fixed — l'autobus, dell'acqua — it is one word with the apostrophe inside it, and it answers for nothing else.

sentences.display: Di solito mi sveglio alle sette
sentences.cue: I usually wake up at seven
sentences.literal: Of usual me I-wake at-the seven

words.note: One key of two words — solito alone is not taught here. It frames the whole sentence, so it goes at the front where English tucks "usually" beside the verb.
Waking is reflexive in Italian. Both halves move together: the pronoun changes with the person and so does the ending — mi sveglio, ti svegli, si sveglia.

sentences.trap: mi is not "myself" here. Nobody wakes themselves up on purpose — Italian simply marks this verb with a pronoun and English leaves it bare, which is why the pronoun is the piece a learner drops.
sentences.sound: dee SO-lee-to mee SVE-lyo. The gli of sveglio is the soft ly of famiglia, not a hard g.

variations.cue: I usually wake up early
variations.changed: the clock time replaced by presto

variations.cue: Do you wake up at seven?

variations.display: Mia sorella si sveglia alle sette
variations.cue: My sister wakes up at seven
variations.changed: the third-person cell, about someone else

mistake.why: The pronoun is part of the verb: Di solito mi sveglio alle sette.

sentences.usage: Saying what your morning normally is — the first thing anyone asks about a routine.
sentences.mnemonic: The pronoun comes first and moves with the person.

sentences.display: Mi alzo, mi lavo e mi vesto
sentences.cue: I get up, I wash and I get dressed
sentences.literal: Me I-raise, me I-wash and me I-dress

words.note: One reflexive verb with its whole paradigm: only the pronoun and the ending move. Without the pronoun, lavare is washing something else — a plate, a car.
Two English words, one Italian verb. vestirsi is an -ire verb, so the loro cell is si vestono — the same set of endings as L1-M6's parto and partire.

sentences.trap: L1-M4's mi alzo is the same shape as the two after it, and the pronoun is repeated on every verb. Italian cannot say it once and let it carry across the list, the way English says "I get up, wash and dress".
sentences.sound: mee AL-tso, mee LA-vo, e mee VES-to. The z of alzo is a hard ts.

variations.cue: I wash and get dressed

variations.display: Si alza, si lava e si veste
variations.cue: He gets up, washes and gets dressed
variations.changed: all three verbs in the third-person cell

variations.cue: We wash and get dressed
variations.changed: the noi cell, where the pronoun is ci

mistake.why: Each verb carries its own pronoun: Mi alzo, mi lavo e mi vesto.

sentences.usage: The three-step opening of almost every account of a day.
sentences.mnemonic: One verb, one pronoun. Never shared.

sentences.display: Poi faccio colazione e prendo l'autobus
sentences.cue: Then I have breakfast and take the bus
sentences.literal: Then I-make breakfast and I-take the-bus

words.note: Italian MAKES breakfast rather than having it: fare colazione, with L1-M6's faccio doing one more of its jobs. It takes no article in the phrase.

sentences.trap: Nothing here is reflexive, and that is worth noticing. Only a verb pointed back at its own subject takes the pronoun; faccio colazione and prendo l'autobus are plain verbs and adding mi would be wrong.
sentences.sound: ko-la-TSYO-ne. The z is a ts and the stress lands on the o.

variations.cue: Then I have breakfast at home
variations.changed: where, instead of what comes next

variations.cue: First I have breakfast, then I go out
I never have breakfast
variations.changed: the negative frequency instead of the sequence

mistake.display: Poi ho colazione e prendo l'autobus
mistake.why: Breakfast is made, not had: Poi faccio colazione e prendo l'autobus.

sentences.usage: The middle of a morning, said in one breath.

words.note: "Never" only works with non in front of the verb: non mangio mai. On its own mai means "ever", which is why the sentence is not negative without the non.

sentences.trap: English forbids the second negative and Italian requires it. non … mai is one word split in two around the verb, and leaving out the non is the commonest mistake in this module.
sentences.sound: mah-ee, one gliding syllable. non runs straight into the verb with no pause.

variations.cue: I never go to the bar
I never drink wine

variations.display: Mia sorella non mangia mai a casa
variations.cue: My sister never eats at home
variations.changed: about someone else, and the non still comes first

mistake.why: The non is compulsory: Non mangio mai a casa.

sentences.usage: Saying what you never do — and the non is what makes it true.
sentences.mnemonic: non before the verb, mai after it.

sentences.display: Vado spesso al bar di mattina
sentences.cue: I often go to the bar in the morning
sentences.literal: I-go often to-the bar of morning

words.note: It sits right after the verb — vado spesso — because it colours the verb rather than framing the sentence. Nothing about it ever changes shape.

sentences.trap: spesso goes after the verb. Vado spesso is the neutral order; Spesso vado is grammatical but front-loads the sentence and makes a listener wait for a contrast that has to arrive.
sentences.sound: SPES-so. Hold the double s — a single one would be a different word entirely.

variations.cue: I often go to the cinema

variations.display: Vado spesso al bar di sera
variations.cue: I often go to the bar in the evening
variations.changed: the evening instead of the morning

variations.display: Mio fratello va spesso al bar
variations.cue: My brother often goes to the bar

mistake.display: Vado spesso al bar in la mattina
mistake.why: The time of day is di: Vado spesso al bar di mattina.

sentences.usage: Reporting a habit with a place in it, the way a neighbour would.

sentences.display: Qualche volta mangio fuori con mia sorella
sentences.cue: Sometimes I eat out with my sister
sentences.literal: Some time I-eat outside with my sister

words.note: One key, and volta alone is not taught here. qualche is always followed by a SINGULAR noun even when the meaning is plural — never *qualche volte.

sentences.trap: qualche volta goes at the front like di solito, because it frames the whole sentence. spesso and mai never can: they belong to the verb and stay beside it.
sentences.sound: KWAL-ke VOL-ta. The che is a hard k, as it always is before e and i.

variations.cue: Sometimes I eat out
Sometimes I go to the seaside
I eat out with my brother
variations.changed: no frequency word at all, and a different person

mistake.why: qualche takes a singular noun: Qualche volta mangio fuori.

sentences.usage: The middle frequency — more than never, less than often.

words.note: The -mente ending is English's -ly, built off the adjective raro. It is the one frequency word here a learner can construct rather than memorise.

words.cue: I go back · I get back
words.note: L1-M10 taught tornare and its participle; this is the plain present. Going home takes a — torno a casa, never in casa.

sentences.trap: raramente can open the sentence like this or sit after the verb — torno raramente a casa tardi. Both are correct Italian; the front position is the emphatic one, and it is the safer place for a learner.
sentences.sound: ra-ra-MEN-te. Every -mente word puts its stress on the men.

variations.cue: I get home late
I rarely go out in the evening
I get home early

mistake.why: Home takes a: Raramente torno a casa tardi.

sentences.usage: Answering how often, when the honest answer is hardly ever.

sentences.display: Ogni lunedì mi riposo a casa
sentences.cue: Every Monday I rest at home
sentences.literal: Every Monday me I-rest at home

words.note: Always with a SINGULAR noun and never with an article: ogni lunedì, not *ogni i lunedì. L1-M4's ogni giorno was this word waiting to be opened.
Resting is reflexive too. Without the pronoun, riposare is what a field or a dough does; the pronoun is what makes it a person taking a rest.

sentences.trap: L1-M4's il lunedì states Mondays as a rule; ogni lunedì counts them one by one. Both are habitual and both are common — the difference is that ogni will not take an article and il lunedì is nothing but one.
sentences.sound: O-nyee loo-ne-DEE. The gn is the ny of onion, and lunedì is stressed on its last syllable.

variations.cue: Every Sunday I rest

variations.display: Il lunedì mi riposo a casa
variations.cue: On Mondays I rest at home
variations.changed: the article form, saying the same thing

variations.display: Mio fratello si riposa a casa
variations.cue: My brother rests at home

mistake.display: Ogni i lunedì mi riposo a casa
mistake.why: ogni never takes an article: Ogni lunedì mi riposo a casa.

sentences.usage: Naming the one day of the week that is different from the rest.

sentences.display: Ci alziamo presto e facciamo colazione
sentences.cue: We get up early and have breakfast
sentences.literal: Us we-raise early and we-make breakfast

words.note: The noi cell of L1-M4's mi alzo. Its pronoun is ci — the same little word as L2-M6's ci vediamo, standing in front of a verb again.
The loro cell. si does double duty here: si alza is one person and si alzano is several, and only the verb ending tells them apart.

sentences.trap: Every reflexive pronoun in this module is a word the course already owns — mi and ti from L2-M5, si from L2-M4, ci from L2-M6. Nothing new is being learned here except where they stand.
sentences.sound: chee al-TSYA-mo. The ci is a soft ch, and alziamo keeps the hard ts of alzo.

variations.cue: We get up early every Monday
variations.changed: a day instead of what comes next

variations.display: Si alzano presto e fanno colazione
variations.cue: They get up early and have breakfast
We get up late on Sundays

mistake.why: The noi pronoun is ci: Ci alziamo presto e facciamo colazione.

sentences.usage: Two people's morning, told as one.
sentences.mnemonic: noi takes ci. loro takes si.

sentences.display: Prima mi lavo, poi mi vesto, infine esco
sentences.cue: First I wash, then I get dressed, finally I go out
sentences.literal: First me I-wash, then me I-dress, at-last I-go-out

words.note: The last item of a list. L2-M10's alla fine says how a story ENDED; infine says a sequence has reached its last step.

sentences.trap: prima and dopo are L2-M4's direction words doing a time job, and neither needs a preposition standing alone like this. Only prima di in front of a verb takes one, and that is not what is happening here.
sentences.sound: een-FEE-ne. Three even syllables with the stress in the middle.

variations.display: Prima mi lavo, poi mi vesto
variations.cue: First I wash, then I get dressed
variations.changed: two steps, with no last one

variations.cue: First I have breakfast, finally I go out

variations.display: Mi lavo, mi vesto e infine esco
variations.cue: I wash, get dressed and finally go out
variations.changed: e instead of the sequencing words

mistake.display: Prima mi lavo, poi mi vesto, finalmente esco
mistake.why: finalmente is relief — at last! The last step of a list is infine: … infine esco.

sentences.usage: A sequence laid out plainly, which is what a routine is.
sentences.mnemonic: infine ends the list. finalmente ends the wait.
